description:
A healthy build reads as a hung one, and the surface built to prevent exactly
that is what misleads.

WHAT HAPPENED, 2026-09-25. Job ...-print_qt6-pdf-905127-patch.job. The operator
saw dsynth_build "running" for well over an hour with a tail frozen on
"SUCCEEDED 00:00:00" and reported the build stuck. It was not. On the host:

  dsynth -S -y -p 2026Q3 test print/qt6-pdf www/qt6-webengine
  dsynth: [01] WORKER build    www/qt6-webengine
  load 12.0 · ninja -j12 · 12 x clang-19 building QtWebEngineCore

print/qt6-pdf is a SLAVE of www/qt6-webengine. dsynth_build adds the master by
itself when `also` is unset (poly-lt5q), so one invocation builds both. The
slave finished at 09:31:35, 11 minutes in. The master -- Chromium -- kept going
for hours.

THE TAIL FOLLOWS THE JOB, NOT THE BUILD

  runner.set_tail_target(env, origin, flavor, job_id, tool)   # the JOB's origin
  dsynth_tail.log_path(env, origin, flavor)                   # that origin's log

`origin` here is the job's. The sibling set lives only inside _dsynth_run's
`build_origins` and is never handed to the tail. So whenever the job's own port
finishes before its siblings -- which is the ordinary case for a small slave of
a large master -- the tail pins to a completed log and stops moving, while
dsynth is at full tilt on a port the page never mentions.

NOTHING ELSE ON THE PAGE NAMES IT EITHER. The now-bar renders
`dsynth_build origin=print/qt6-pdf`, because `also` was resolved INSIDE the
tool rather than passed as an argument -- the model never wrote it, so the
tool-call args cannot show it. An operator has no way, anywhere in the console,
to learn that qt6-webengine is what they are waiting for.

COST, and it is not theoretical. The operator read it as stuck. So did I: I
filed poly-5qtr against an unbounded subprocess and proposed adding timeouts to
a tool whose legitimate runtime is hours, then took a second wrong turn into a
pipe-EOF theory. Every measurement was correct; the assumption that "the log"
meant "the build" was not, and nothing available on the tracker could have
corrected it. It took a shell on the builder.

WHAT TO FIX, roughly in order of what it buys

1. TAIL WHAT DSYNTH IS BUILDING. The invocation knows its origin list; pass it
   to set_tail_target and follow the newest log among them, or better, the one
   dsynth's worker is on. Then the tail keeps moving through the whole
   invocation and the frozen-log state disappears.
2. SAY WHICH PORTS ARE IN THE RUN. `built_origins` is already on the result and
   arrives too late -- the operator needs it while it runs. The now-bar's tool
   line is the place: `dsynth_build origin=print/qt6-pdf +www/qt6-webengine`.
3. MAKE "NOT MOVING" LEGIBLE. poly-qqx9.8 put "last line N ago" on the page for
   precisely this question and it rendered as an em-dash throughout the
   incident -- the JS fills .tail-ago from data-mtime and the value WAS present
   (1790328695.637114). Worth finding out why it never painted; a tail that had
   said "last line 1h18m ago" would have raised the right question immediately
   instead of the wrong one.

RELATED
  poly-1v7l  the same job's flavor holds its origin, which makes log_path fall
             through to "newest by mtime" -- a second way the tail can land on
             a log nobody asked for.
  poly-5qtr  the wrong diagnosis, closed, kept for the reasoning.
notes:
THE TWO FILES, SIDE BY SIDE, 11:18:57Z
/root/.cache/dports-dev/envs/2026Q3/root/work/dsynth/logs

  -rw-r--r--  root  wheel   3,388,985  Sep 25 09:31  print___qt6-pdf.log
  -rw-r--r--  root  wheel  47,245,874  Sep 25 11:18  www___qt6-webengine.log

The page tails the first: 3.4 MB, untouched for 1h47m. dsynth is writing the
second: 47 MB, growing this minute, fourteen times the size of the one on
screen. One invocation, both logs, and the console follows the wrong one for
as long as the master takes.

Also settles poly-1v7l as latent rather than live here: the filename is plain
`print___qt6-pdf.log` with no @flavor suffix, so the unmatchable name the bad
flavor builds falls through to candidates[0] and lands on the same file it
would have chosen anyway. It bites when a port has more than one flavor log.
title: The dsynth tail follows the job's origin while the build runs a sibling set, so a finished slave freezes the tail and a healthy build reads as hung

close_reason: not a defect: the build is healthy, the tail was showing a sibling's finished log
description:
LIVE INCIDENT, 2026-09-25. Job
20260925-091002Z-2026Q3-print_qt6-pdf-905127-patch.job, attempt 1, turn 41.
dsynth_build has shown "running" since 09:20:13Z and had not returned 45
minutes later, while the build's own log says it finished.

WHAT THE TRACKER SHOWS, measured rather than guessed

  runner heartbeat   healthy -- sampled every 15s, 1s old each time. So the
                     PROCESS is alive and the heartbeat thread is ticking on
                     its 5s interval. Only the main thread is stuck.
  tool               dsynth_build, since 2026-09-25T09:20:13Z
  published tail     frozen at 3,388,985 bytes across five samples over two
                     minutes, last line `SUCCEEDED 00:00:00`, preceded by
                     `rcng_ldconfig: Operation not permitted` twice and a
                     `Deleting files for qt6-pdf-6.11.1` counter run to 100%
  turn               41, unmoved

The log is not growing and ends in dsynth's own success line. The tool call
outlives the build it is waiting for.

THE CALL HAS NO BOUND

  worker._dsynth_run()       p = _exec(env, "/bin/sh", "-c", cmd, "_", *origins)
  worker._exec(...)          subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True,
                                            timeout=timeout)   # timeout=None

_exec TAKES a timeout parameter and NOT ONE CALLER PASSES IT -- every
chroot-bound tool in worker.py goes through it, and `grep -c timeout` over the
call sites returns 0. There is no tool-timeout setting either; settings.py
bounds llm.*.timeout and delivery.git_timeout and nothing else. So a dsynth
that never exits blocks the runner's main thread for as long as the process
lives, holding the one runner and its claimed job.

WHY IT PROBABLY OUTLIVED DSYNTH ITSELF. capture_output=True means
subprocess.run reads stdout/stderr to EOF, and EOF comes when the LAST holder
of the pipe closes it -- not when dsynth exits. Anything dsynth left behind
inside the chroot that inherited those descriptors keeps the read blocked
after dsynth is gone. `rcng_ldconfig: Operation not permitted` immediately
before the success line says an rc script ran during package registration,
which is the kind of thing that leaves a process behind.

That last paragraph is the HYPOTHESIS and is not yet confirmed; it needs the
host. Two cheap checks settle it:

  ps -auxww | grep -E 'dsynth|dev-env exec'   is dsynth gone, defunct, or
                                              still running?
  fstat -p <runner pid>                       who else holds the pipe?

CONFIRMED EITHER WAY: an unbounded wait on a build. Whether dsynth hung or its
pipe outlived it, nothing in the runner can end it.

THE FIX
  * a timeout on the dsynth calls at least. The parameter is already there and
    already threaded; today it is simply never given a value.
  * do not wait on the pipe for the verdict. For the long tools, wait on the
    PROCESS and drain the pipes separately, so a lingering descriptor holder
    cannot outlive the exit status. The tail already gives the operator the
    output live, so the captured stream is no longer the only way to see it.
  * a stuck tool should be visible. Nothing on the job page distinguishes "a
    44-minute build is running" from "this returned 45 minutes ago and we are
    still waiting" -- the tail's own mtime is the signal, and poly-qqx9.8 put
    "last line N ago" on the page for exactly this. It rendered blank here;
    worth checking why, because it would have named this in one glance.

RELATED
  poly-q07p -- abandoning the job leaves the .job file claimable, so the
  runner re-claims it. That constrains the recovery for this incident.
  poly-xxys -- the same class of defect on the heartbeat thread, latent.
notes:
THE LOG'S OWN MTIME SETTLES THE HALF OF THIS THAT COULD BE SETTLED REMOTELY.
The runner publishes it with every tail; the page carries it as
`<pre class="tool-tail" data-mtime=...>`.

  09:20:13Z  dsynth_build tool call starts
  09:31:35Z  the dsynth log is written for the LAST time, ending
             "SUCCEEDED 00:00:00"
  10:49Z     still running. 1h18m since anything touched that file.

Two consequences.

FIRST, the build is over. It ran 11m22s and produced 3,388,985 bytes, nearly
all of it a "Deleting files for qt6-pdf-6.11.1" progress counter; the zero
duration on the success line says dsynth found little to do beyond replacing
the package. The tool call has now outlived its own build by seven times the
build's length.

SECOND, it rules out the competing explanation. This job's `flavor` is stored
as "print/qt6-pdf" -- the origin duplicated into the flavor field, which is
wrong, and which makes dsynth_tail.log_path build an unmatchable filename
("print___qt6-pdf@print/qt6-pdf.log") and fall through to candidates[0], the
NEWEST log by mtime. So the obvious alternative was that the page is showing a
stale log while a real build runs elsewhere. It is not: the newest
print___qt6-pdf*.log was last written at 09:31:35, so no dsynth log for this
port has been written in 78 minutes. dsynth is not building.

(The flavor corruption is real and worth its own bead -- it is a latent
wrong-log bug that only failed to bite here because there was one candidate.)

WHAT IS STILL UNKNOWN, and needs the host: whether dsynth is alive and hung
after printing its success line, or gone with its stdout/stderr held open by
something it left behind. `ps -auxww | grep -E 'dsynth|dev-env exec'` and
`fstat -p <runner pid>` separate the two. The pipe reading is the more likely
of the two, and the log's last lines point at it -- two `rcng_ldconfig:
Operation not permitted` immediately before the success line say an rc script
ran during package registration inside the chroot, which is exactly the kind
of thing that leaves a descendant holding the inherited descriptors.

Either way the fix is the same and is already stated above: bound the call,
and wait on the process rather than on EOF.
WRONG. Nothing is hung. Closing as not-a-defect, with the diagnosis corrected
in full because the reasoning failed in an instructive way.

WHAT THE HOST SHOWS (2026-09-25 11:13Z, ssh antonioh@the builder):

  root 914381  dsynth -S -y -p 2026Q3 test print/qt6-pdf www/qt6-webengine
  root 920594  dsynth: [01] WORKER build    www/qt6-webengine

  load averages: 12.02, 12.16, 12.27
  /usr/local/bin/ninja -j12 -v -C /construction/www/qt6-webengine/.build/
      src/core/Release/x86_64 QtWebEngineCore
  12 x clang-19

ONE dsynth invocation, TWO ports. print/qt6-pdf is a SLAVE of
www/qt6-webengine, and dsynth_build adds the master itself:

    if also is None:
        also = invariant_origins(env, origin)[1:]

"Left unset it resolves to the port's patch origin -- for a slave, the master
whose dragonfly/ the fix was written into -- so the agent loop proves both
halves of the thing it just changed" (poly-lt5q).

So the slave finished in 11m22s at 09:31:35, and the master -- Chromium -- has
been compiling ever since and will be for hours. The call is unbounded because
the work is unbounded. That is correct behaviour.

WHY I CONCLUDED OTHERWISE, since the evidence was real and the reading was not.
Every measurement in this bead was true: the log's last write WAS 09:31:35, it
DID end in SUCCEEDED, and the tool call HAS outlived it. What I never
questioned was the assumption underneath -- that "the log" meant "the build".
The tail resolves from the JOB's origin, and the invocation was building
something the job's origin does not name. The page shows a finished log while
dsynth works on a port nothing on screen mentions. Every symptom follows from
that one substitution, and no amount of further remote measurement could have
corrected it: the missing fact was not on the tracker at all.

THE RECOMMENDATION WAS ALSO WRONG. "Bound the call" would put a timeout on a
tool whose legitimate runtime is measured in hours; any value large enough for
qt6-webengine is too large to catch a real hang. Timeouts are not the answer
here.

WHAT IS REAL, and carries forward to poly-6bv7: an operator cannot distinguish
a long build from a stopped one, and the tail -- the surface built to answer
exactly that -- pointed at the wrong port.

(The pipe-EOF theory was never tested and is not supported: dsynth is alive
and working. poly-xxys stands on its own, unaffected.)
The real bead is poly-quu3 (the id named above was written before it existed).
title: A dsynth build that never returns hangs the runner forever: no tool call passes _exec's timeout

description:
DIVERGENCE FROM THE DESIGN SOURCE, found by the operator 2026-09-24.

The epic names artifact "Five Ways to Watch a Job" version 9 as what the work
is measured against. Re-read today. It carries DEDICATED TERMINAL TOKENS that
are dark in BOTH themes:

  light   --term-bg #0e161d  --term-fg #c8d4dc  --term-dim #6c7f8d
  dark    --term-bg #05090d  --term-fg #c8d4dc  --term-dim #5d6e7b

  .tt-tail { color: var(--term-fg); background: var(--term-bg); height: 132px; }
  .tt-tail .dim { color: var(--term-dim); }
  .tt-tailbar { color: var(--faint); background: var(--head); font: 11px mono; }

What was built uses --code-fg on --code-bg, which in the light theme is
#253039 on #f6f8fa: a CODE BLOCK, the same treatment as a tool stdout dump.
The design deliberately distinguishes the two -- .tt pre uses --code-bg and
.tt-tail uses --term-bg, in the same specimen, ten lines apart. progress.css
has no --term-* tokens at all, so the divergence was introduced when the tail
CSS was first written and survived because nobody compared.

SECOND DEFECT, same element: THE TAIL MUST SIT ON THE LAST LINE unless the
reader has scrolled up. Half-implemented in poly-pvs2: agentic-job.js pins to
the bottom when it SWAPS the slot on a poll, but nothing scrolls it on the
initial server render, so first paint shows the oldest of the last forty lines
next to a label reading "last line 4s ago".

FIX
- add --term-bg / --term-fg / --term-dim to all three token blocks in
  progress.css (bare :root, the prefers-color-scheme guard, and
  :root[data-theme="dark"]), matching the design values
- .tool-tail takes --term-fg on --term-bg
- scroll the tail to the bottom on initial load as well as on swap
notes:
ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM THE DESIGN SURVIVES, written down per the
repo rule rather than left to be rediscovered.

The design sets .tt-tail at font: 11.5px/1.5. This sheet has an
accessibility floor of 12px, enforced by
test_design_tokens.py::test_nothing_essential_is_below_twelve_pixels, which
was added after a 10px uppercase label slipped in (UI-4). A running builds
log is precisely the essential text that floor exists to protect, so the
rule wins and the tail is 12px.

Everything else matches the source: --term-bg / --term-fg / --term-dim at the
designs values in all three token blocks, and height 132px rather than the
max-height it had (a pane that resizes under the reader as lines arrive gives
scroll-to-bottom no stable frame).
title: The dsynth tail is a code block, not a terminal, and it opens on the oldest line

description:
FOUND IN DEPLOYMENT 2026-09-24, and it hid a whole feature.

server.py computes static_v as the sha256 of progress.css alone -- its comment
says so: "Content-hash cache-buster for progress.css". Both the CSS and the JS
tags then interpolate that one token:

  _base.html:23          progress.css?v={{ static_v }}
  agentic_job.html:176   agentic-job.js?v={{ static_v }}
  agentic_job_transcript.html:51   same

So a change to any .js file does not move the token. The URL is byte-identical,
every warm browser cache keeps the old script, and there is no error anywhere --
the server sends the new payload and the stale client ignores the parts it does
not know about.

OBSERVED: poly-pvs2 shipped a tail_html slot plus the JS that swaps it. On the
builder the producer published correctly and the tracker returned tail_html on
every poll, verified by curl. The page showed nothing, because the browser was
running agentic-job.js from before the deploy. progress.css was untouched by
that work -- the tail CSS had survived poly-paee -- so the token was unchanged.

There are 9 files in static/ (196K total), 5 of them .js. Any JS-only change
has always shipped this way.

FIX: hash the whole static directory, including each file relative path so a
rename or deletion also moves the token. One directory read at startup.
notes:
FIXED 2026-09-24. static_v is now the sha256 of every file under static/, each
files relative path hashed alongside its bytes so a rename or deletion moves
the token too. One directory read at startup; static/ is 196K across 9 files.

Test pins it as a CONTRACT rather than by re-running the loop: the token the
app serves must equal the hash of the whole tree. Mutation-checked -- reverting
to progress.css alone fails that test, which is the bug as it shipped. Five more
cover a JS-only change, a CSS-only change, a rename, that every versioned tag
carries the token, and that the page still serves one.

WHY THE OLD TEST SUITE COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THIS: nothing asserted on the
tokens INPUTS, only that a token existed. The defect is invisible server-side --
correct HTML, correct payload, correct headers - and shows up only in a browser
that already has the file. That is also why poly-pvs2 passed 31 tests and still
showed nothing on the builder.
title: Static cache-buster is the CSS's hash, so a JS-only change ships invisibly

description:
Reported from a running job, 2026-09-24: the attempt number and turn show
briefly, then vanish while the job is still live and refreshing.

A contract mismatch between the fragment and its client.

api_job_activity_fragment renders every body `if rows else ""`, where
`rows` is only the rows NEWER than the client's cursor. The client does:

  if (data.nowbar_html !== undefined && barSlot)
      barSlot.innerHTML = data.nowbar_html;

An empty string passes `!== undefined`, so the first poll with nothing new
assigns "" and ERASES the bar. startElapsedClock() then has nothing to
tick. The cards survive the same poll only because their guard is
`if (data.cards_html && ...)` -- truthiness, which "" fails.

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE "A SHORT PERIOD OF TIME": rows arrive in bursts at turn
boundaries and vanish in between. A long tool emits nothing for its whole
duration -- a 41-minute dsynth build is 41 minutes of empty polls -- so the
bar disappears exactly during the wait it exists to explain.

The client's guard was written expecting the key to be OMITTED when there
is nothing new; the server sends "" instead. Fix on the server so the
deliberate clear still works: when a poll HAS rows and now_bar() returns
None (MANUAL tier, or the job just ended), "" is correct and must still
empty the slot.

Not a re-render problem: with no new rows the bar's content cannot have
changed (no new turn, no new tool), and the elapsed clock is client-side.
Omitting the key is both correct and free.
notes:
FIXED 2026-09-24.

The fragment now OMITS nowbar_html when no rows are new, rather than
sending "". The client's guard was already written for that contract; the
server was the half that disagreed.

Deliberately a presence check, not truthiness: on a poll that HAS rows,
now_bar() returning None (MANUAL tier, or the job just ended) must still
empty the slot, and truthiness would have kept a stale bar on screen
forever.

No client change. Hardening the JS to ignore "" as well would have broken
that deliberate clear, so the contract is stated in a comment at the
server instead -- one reader, one writer, one rule.

Nothing is lost by omitting it: with no new rows there is no new turn and
no new tool, so the bar's content cannot have changed, and the elapsed
clock runs client-side off a data attribute.

cards_html was never affected because its client guard is truthiness
(`if (data.cards_html && ...)`), which "" fails. That inconsistency is why
only the bar disappeared and the cards stayed -- matching the report.

Test: a poll at the newest cursor returns changed:false and no
nowbar_html key at all. 4210 pass.
title: The now-bar disappears on a live job: the fragment sends an empty bar when nothing is new

description:
poly-qqx9.8 put a running build's last lines inside the tool row that was
running it. As built it cannot work: the tracker resolves the log path
through worker._dsynth_log_candidates -> env_paths() -> a root-only
`dev-env path`, and the tracker is unprivileged. poly-paee removes the
wiring. This bead holds the decision about what, if anything, replaces it.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST "DO WHAT THE DIFF DOES". The diff publishes once per
attempt; the tail's whole value is sub-minute freshness during a 41-minute
build. Over the artifact channel that means the runner re-POSTing the last
~32 KiB every N seconds -- put_blob upserts on (bundle_id, relpath) and is
content-addressed, so an unchanged tail costs no new blob, but it is still
a periodic emitter inside the build wait loop, which is a change to the
loop rather than a tracker fix.

THREE OPTIONS, in the order I would consider them:
1. The runner publishes a rolling tail artifact every N seconds while a
   tailable tool runs. Honest, reuses the existing channel, and the
   dsynth_tail.read_tail windowing/offset/cap logic is reusable as the
   producer side.
2. Drop the feature. The full log already reaches the tracker as
   logs/full.log.gz when the build ENDS, and the tool row already shows
   the build running with an elapsed clock. The tail was a nicety.
3. Leave it for poly-fij, where a remote runner needs a general answer for
   streaming progress anyway, and a bespoke tail channel would be work
   thrown away.

What must NOT happen is the current state: a feature that looks built,
renders nothing, and says nothing about why.
notes:
SEQUENCED AFTER poly-fij.4, 2026-09-24. Not frozen for lack of a mechanism
any more -- frozen because the mechanism needs a channel that does not exist
yet.

THE TIMER PROBLEM IS SOLVED, and option 1's cost estimate above was wrong.
It said a periodic emitter would mean a background thread or a Popen rewrite
of the build path. The runner ALREADY has one: _heartbeat_loop, a daemon
thread started at runner.py:2081, ticking every HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL = 5s.
Verified live on a builder -- host clock 10:38:18Z against
runner_status.updated_at 10:38:16.599, two seconds old -- and it keeps
ticking through a build because it is a separate thread from the one blocked
in subprocess.run. Nothing in _dsynth_run needs touching.

It does not need dev-env exec either. The runner is root, so it can resolve
env_paths(env).writable / "work/dsynth/logs/..." and open the file directly:
a host-side read, no chroot spawn per tick. The offset-seeking reader for
exactly this is recoverable at commit 6275522; it was only ever wrong in the
TRACKER, where resolving the path needed root.

THE DESTINATION IS THE PROBLEM. The obvious cheap store -- a few columns on
runners or runner_status, overwritten in place, which the heartbeat is
already writing in the same transaction -- would be a TENTH direct sqlite
write from the runner, on precisely the channel poly-fij.4 exists to remove.
Storing it as artifacts instead is not an alternative: a tail's bytes differ
every tick, so nothing dedupes, and 480 ticks over a 40-minute build is
~15 MB per build and several GB across the jobs already run. A tail wants
one overwritten row, and the runner should not be writing rows.

So: heartbeat as the timer, and the tail rides the HTTP write channel
poly-fij.4 establishes -- most likely on the heartbeat endpoint itself,
since that is the one call already happening at the right cadence with the
right identity. That is option 3 of the three above, reached from the other
direction.

ALSO NOT FREE, and still unmeasured: a 32 KiB seek-read every 5s per running
build. If it matters the tail can tick on a multiple of the heartbeat
without changing anything else.

MEANWHILE, and independent of all of it: a failed dsynth_build row could
link to its bundle's logs/errors.txt (21,938 bytes on one measured job) and
logs/full.log.gz, which already exist and are already rendered by the
artifact viewer. That is one click from the row that failed instead of two
clicks and knowing where to look, it needs no runner change at all, and it
is most of the practical value. It does not solve liveness -- only a real
tail does.
DEPENDENCY CORRECTED 2026-09-24. Was poly-fij.4 (auth); that was wrong. Auth is not on this bead's path: the five existing /v1 routes carry no credential, the runner already POSTs to them unauthenticated over loopback, and internet exposure is deferred. When poly-fij.4 lands it adds a header to the whole channel at once, the tail included.

The real blocker is poly-fij.12, and specifically only its first two steps. The note above says the tail should ride 'the heartbeat endpoint itself, since that is the one call already happening at the right cadence with the right identity' -- there is no such endpoint. /v1 has artifacts/get, artifacts/put, bundles/upsert, jobs/transition, user-context. Creating POST /v1/runners/heartbeat is poly-fij.12 step 2, and its own description calls that step 'self-contained -- proves the path end to end at trivial volume'.

So: poly-fij.12 steps 1-2 (the seam, then the heartbeat), then this. Steps 3-5 of that bead (activity_log batching, issues, the reads) are the rest of the epic and are NOT needed here.

poly-fij.7 is NOT on this path either, contrary to an earlier reading. The relay exists because the HOOKS only know 127.0.0.1. The tail's producer is the runner, which reaches the tracker directly.

STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: the renderer is already built and tested -- running_tailable_tool and attach_tool_tail in tracker/render/activity.py, four tests in test_render_tool_tail.py, both carrying 'Has no caller in production'. Only the wiring is missing. The offset reader is at commit 6275522. _dsynth_log_candidates (worker.py) resolves the path root-side.

ONE GAP MEASURED: the heartbeat can see _current_job_id and _current_stage (runner.py:292-293) but not env+origin, which the path resolver needs. Two more module globals, set where _current_stage is.
CODE READ 2026-09-24. THE FEATURE IS SMALLER THAN THIS BEAD ASSUMES, and one part is bigger.

1. THE WHOLE VIEW LAYER SURVIVED poly-paee. Not just the two render helpers:
   _turn_cards.html         the tail block, tailbar, byte counts, log link
   progress.css:2633        .tool-tail / .tool-tailbar
   agentic-job.js:274       the 'last line N ago' ticker off data-mtime
   render/activity.py       running_tailable_tool + attach_tool_tail, 4 tests
poly-paee removed only the PRODUCER -- tracker/dsynth_tail.py, the route, and
the pages.py wiring. So this is a producer plus a sink plus re-attaching one
call, not a feature rebuild.

2. THE OFFSET READER IS REUSABLE VERBATIM, and it belongs on the runner now.
git show 6275522:dportsv3/tracker/dsynth_tail.py -- (path, offset) -> (text,
next offset, eof), nothing host-specific, delegating to
worker._dsynth_log_candidates. It was only ever wrong because it ran in the
TRACKER, which cannot resolve a dev-env path. On the runner, which is root,
it is correct as written. Moving it to dportsv3/agent/.

NO OFFSET TRACKING, though. Incremental reads would leave the row holding only
what arrived in the last tick -- zero lines on a quiet build. The page wants
the newest screenful every time, so the producer reads offset=-1,
max_lines=40 each tick and overwrites. That is a 32 KiB seek-read per tick,
still unmeasured, as this bead already flagged.

3. THE LIVE PATH IS THE PART THIS BEAD MISSED, and it is the same defect as
poly-qqx9.16 one surface over. In agentic_api.py the fragment computes
    window = activity_for_job(...) if rows else []
    cards  = group_activity_into_cards(window) if rows else []
and returns changed=bool(rows). A dsynth build writes NO activity_log rows for
40 minutes, so with the tail hung on a card the live view would never refresh
it -- exactly what the attempt strip's own comment says it fixed for itself:
'Gated on new rows it would sit frozen for the whole of a long build'.

Fixing it by ungating the card render would swap the whole card container every
3s for the length of a build, which recreates the tail's <pre> and so resets
the scroll position of the one element a reader may be scrolled inside. So the
tail gets ITS OWN SLOT, like strip_html and worktree_html: _tool_tail.html
extracted as a partial, sent as tail_html, swapped in place with the scroll
preserved.

THE SINK IS KEYED BY RUNNER, NOT BY JOB. One row per job would be unbounded
over time at up to 32 KiB each -- the artifact-growth objection this bead
already makes, just slower. Keyed by runner_id it is exactly N rows forever,
with job_id as a column: the page reads WHERE job_id = ? and correctly gets
nothing once that builder moved on, which is also the right semantics, since a
finished job's tail is superseded by logs/full.log.gz.

THE LOG LINK HAS NO TARGET WHILE RUNNING. The template's 'open the whole log'
href pointed at api_job_dsynth_tail, which poly-paee deleted, and full.log.gz
does not exist until the build ends. Guarded in the template rather than
rendered as an empty href.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-24. Option 1 of the three, reached with poly-fij.12's carrier instead of a bespoke channel -- so the answer to 'or it goes' is that it stays.

  agent/dsynth_tail.py      the offset reader, moved from tracker/ unchanged.
                            It was never wrong -- only in the wrong process.
  runner._tail_target       what to tail, or None. Set at tool_start for a
                            TAILABLE tool, cleared when any call returns.
  runner._heartbeat_tail()  offset=-1, max_lines=40, never raises.
  presence.set_tail         one row per builder, overwritten; NULLs when
                            nothing runs; also blanked on deregister.
  runner_tail               new table, PK runner_id, job_id a column.
  job_tail(conn, job_id)    WHERE job_id = ? AND text IS NOT NULL.
  _tool_tail.html           the block extracted as a partial.
  tail_html                 its own slot, sent on EVERY poll.
  common/tools.py           TAILABLE_TOOLS declared once, both sides import.

4267 -> 4298 tests (31 new, two files).

MUTATION-CHECKED, the one that matters: gating the fragment's tail read on
 -- i.e. reintroducing the defect described above -- fails three tests
including test_the_tail_refreshes_with_no_new_activity_rows. Without that the
feature would have looked built and been frozen for the length of every build,
which is the exact failure mode this bead was filed to prevent.

FOUR THINGS THE REVIEW ADDED:
- Follow the newest line. A live tail whose <pre> is recreated every 3s renders
  scrolled to the TOP, showing the oldest of the last forty lines beside a
  label reading 'last line 4s ago'. It now pins to the bottom unless the reader
  has scrolled up.
- The swap runs AFTER the cards swap, since the slot lives inside the card
  stream and would otherwise be overwritten on any poll that had rows.
- deregister blanks the tail. The page's 'is a tool running' gate reads
  activity rows, and a stopped runner leaves those looking like a live build.
  A crash cannot run it; there the mtime ticker counting up is the tell.
- No 'open the whole log' link. It pointed at a route poly-paee deleted, and
  full.log.gz does not exist until the build ends -- href="" reads as broken.

COVERAGE: patch and convert both, since both run through PatchAttemptStep's
dispatcher. Triage has its own handler and nothing to tail -- it reads a log
that already exists rather than producing one.

STILL UNMEASURED, as this bead said: a 32 KiB seek-read every 5s per running
build. If it shows up, the tail can tick on a multiple of the heartbeat without
touching anything else -- _heartbeat_tail() is the only place that would change.

THE MEANWHILE ITEM IS NOT DONE and is now separable: a FAILED dsynth_build row
linking to its bundle's logs/errors.txt and logs/full.log.gz. That is about
finished builds, needs no runner change, and is worth its own bead.
CORRECTION to the note above: one word was lost to shell quoting. The mutation was "gating the fragment tail read on ROWS" -- that is, on new activity_log rows since the cursor, exactly as everything else in that fragment is gated.
title: Freeze: the dsynth tail needs the runner to publish it, or it goes

description:
Found on a live builder, 2026-09-24. The tracker must never run anything;
the runner may be remote (poly-fij), so anything that reaches into a build
environment is wrong by construction, not merely broken today.

TWO VIOLATIONS, both introduced by poly-qqx9 and the only two in the
package. There is no subprocess/Popen/os.system anywhere in
dportsv3/tracker/, and every other agent import is lifecycle (pure
constants) or fix_chat/llm (an outbound API call):

  tracker/worktree_source.py:52   from dportsv3.agent import worker
  tracker/dsynth_tail.py:133      from dportsv3.agent import worker

Both die as the unprivileged tracker account:

  from_workspace -> worker.emit_diff -> env_paths()
                 -> `dportsv3 dev-env path` -> require_root()   cli.py:282
                 -> _exec -> `dev-env exec`  -> require_root()   cli.py:811
  dsynth_tail.log_path -> worker._dsynth_log_candidates -> env_paths()

Verified on the host: the tracker service runs as `polytropos`, the runner
as root; chroot as non-root is EPERM; no sudoers grant for the tracker
user; no DPORTS_DEV_ENV_CMD in its rc.d script. from_workspace's bare
`except Exception` swallows all of it, so the working-tree band renders
nothing and the tail reports "no log" -- silently, on every job.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT CAUSE for the band being absent. The finished-job
fallback reads analysis/rescued/<job_id>.diff, which the rescue path
writes only when the harness RAISES. On the live builder:

  analysis/rescued/%    4 rows
  %changes.diff       289 rows

analysis/changes.diff is the canonical artifact every patch job writes
(runner._write_changes_diff). It was passed over because changes.diff is
per-BUNDLE and a retried bundle's copy may belong to a later job -- which
is true, and cost the band ~99% of the jobs it could have rendered.

SCOPE HERE: stop executing, and read artifacts only. Delete the worker
call in worktree_source; fall back to analysis/changes.diff, labelled,
since it may be a sibling job's; remove the tracker's live-tail wiring.

A running job then has no diff to show until the runner publishes one,
which is the follow-up -- and it must SAY that rather than render nothing.
notes:
FIXED 2026-09-24. The tracker no longer runs anything.

worktree_source.from_workspace is DELETED, not repaired, and the module no
longer imports agent.worker. A test asserts the absence -- no
from_workspace attribute, no worker import, no subprocess in the file --
because the next person to want a live diff will reach for exactly this.

THE BAND NOW READS THE CANONICAL ARTIFACT. Order is rescued (per job,
exact) then analysis/changes.diff (per bundle, 289 on a live builder
against 4 rescued). The per-bundle one is LABELLED "from the bundle's
diff", with a title saying a retried bundle may share it between jobs --
the precision loss is stated rather than hidden, which is what made
preferring the exact artifact and showing nothing the wrong trade.

A PATCH JOB WITH NOTHING PUBLISHED SAYS SO: #worktree-pending, "no diff
published yet", and one line explaining the runner publishes when the
attempt ends. An absent band reads as "changed nothing". Only for type
patch -- on a triage or verify job it would be noise about work that job
never does.

THE TAIL WIRING IS GONE: tracker/dsynth_tail.py deleted, the
/api/jobs/<id>/dsynth-tail route deleted, and the read dropped from both
the job page and the live fragment. The reader is recoverable at commit
6275522 if poly-pvs2 takes the publish option.

render.running_tailable_tool and attach_tool_tail STAY, and say in their
own docstrings that they have no producer. They are pure, they are what any
publisher would feed, and the pairing they encode -- only a long tool gets
a tail, it hangs on the running row -- is the part worth not rediscovering.
Their tests moved to tests/test_render_tool_tail.py; the reader's 11 tests
went with the reader.

WHAT IS STILL NOT VISIBLE, and needs the runner: a RUNNING job's diff.
poly-5tgc. Until then a running patch job shows the pending note and a
finished one shows its diff, which is 289 jobs more than before.

4203 tests pass.
title: The tracker executes runner-side code, so the working tree and the dsynth tail are dead in deployment

description:
Found against a live builder's state.db, 2026-09-24.

activity_log is a GLOBAL rolling cap: runner.activity_log_max (default
5000), enforced by a DELETE in runner.py:1877. Observed on a live host:
one day of rows, ids 65074-70073, 5000 rows, and 3 DISTINCT JOBS out of
1,452 in the database (364 patch, 600 triage, 187 verify, 301 confirm).
A patch job spends roughly 1,600 rows, so the page holds about the last
three jobs.

Every surface poly-qqx9 added reads activity_log: the now-bar, the
attempt strip, the turn cards, the working-tree band. On an evicted job
they do not degrade, they assert -- a now-bar with nothing running, a
strip with no attempts, no turn cards at all, on a job that really did
run seven attempts. The old flat table had the same hole; the epic turned
one empty table into five positive claims.

The obligation is already assigned to this page. jobs.py:421 keeps
intra-job attempt detail OFF the occurrence aggregate for exactly this
reason: "a number that silently becomes 0 when it is evicted is worse
than no number. That detail stays on the job page, where the caveat is
local." No job-page template states it.

THE SIGNAL IS EXACT, so this needs no heuristic. jobs and job_events are
never pruned (jobs.py:415). A job whose job_events show that it ran,
which has no activity_log rows, and whose last transition predates
SELECT MIN(ts) FROM activity_log, has been pruned. One extra query.

Three states have to read differently, which is the whole bug:
pruned, nothing-yet (a job just claimed), and has-activity.

DEEPER QUESTION, DELIBERATELY NOT A BLOCKER: the cap is global, so one
chatty patch job (2,130 llm_turn rows in the observed window) evicts
every other job's history. Per-job retention, or simply a larger cap, is
a runner-side change with a disk cost. The page misreporting is a bug
whichever way that lands, so fix the page first.
notes:
FIXED 2026-09-24. THE DESCRIPTION OVERSTATED THE SYMPTOM, and the real one is narrower and worse. The five surfaces do NOT assert: _attempt_strip.html guards on {% if strip and strip.attempts %}, _job_activity.html on {% if activity_cards %}, now_bar returns None without turns, and the working tree carries an `empty` flag. They all go quiet correctly. What asserted was one sentence, in the else branch nobody reads:
No activity recorded for this job.
False for every evicted job, and on a live builder that is 1,449 of 1,452. Said beside a durable transitions table showing seven attempts, which is what makes it read as a tracker fault rather than a retention policy. THREE STATES NOW READ DIFFERENTLY, which was the acceptance criterion: - pruned, nothing left -> "Activity has aged out", naming the cap, the oldest row the log still holds, when this job started, and that the lifecycle transitions are durable. - nothing yet -> the original sentence, unchanged. - partly pruned -> a note above the surviving cards. This is the worst case and was not in the original description: the survivors look like the whole story and the attempt strip counts only them. activity_pruning(conn, job_id) asks the two durable sources (jobs and job_events are never pruned) and FAILS CLOSED: with an empty activity_log there is no horizon, so it reports not-pruned rather than announcing pruning it cannot demonstrate. It says "any activity it recorded", never "its activity". Whether a job emitted activity at all is unknowable once the rows are gone, and a verify or confirm job may legitimately have emitted none -- the same uncertainty that made poly-qqx9.1's Q2 unanswerable. THE TRANSCRIPT ROUTE HAD THE SAME SENTENCE and now shares one partial, _activity_pruned.html, so the two wordings cannot drift. It is the surface that claims to be the WHOLE transcript, so the remnant note matters more there. One defect caught before it shipped: the transcript builds its template context AFTER its `with _conn()` block closes, so the query had to move inside the block rather than being a call in the dict. The global-vs-per-job cap question is untouched and still open -- see the description. The page is honest now whichever way that lands. 4209 tests pass; 8 new in tests/test_activity_pruning.py.
title: Job page presents a pruned activity log as a job where nothing happened
